**4B.5 Research Note**
**Working verdict:** **mixed, leaning no**. I found several signs of institutionalized governance and limited deference to formal bodies, but also persistent red-tagging, coercive information pressure, and security-force involvement in intimidation. I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of a classic personality cult or explicit loyalty-test regime, but I also did not find evidence that Marcos systematically kept neutral institutions free from politicization.

| Direction | Claim-level item | Source | Date | URL | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive / mixed | Marcos opened 2024 by branding the administration as “Bagong Pilipinas.” That is self-presentation and political branding, but the source does not show a full personality cult or leader-worship campaign. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-01-28 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-ushers-filipinos-to-a-bagong-pilipinas-that-serves-its-people/ | 4B.5 |
| Positive | Marcos told critics to let Comelec handle allegations that signatures in the people’s initiative drive may have been bought. That is modest deference to an election body rather than direct executive capture. | GMA News Online | 2024-01-23 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/895067/marcos-on-people-s-initiative-for-cha-cha-let-comelec-do-their-job/story/ | 4B.5, 4B.4, 4B.1 |
| Positive / mixed | Marcos publicly pledged a free and safe environment for journalists and said critical press is better than cooperative press. That cuts against overt intimidation of neutral media institutions, at least at the level of rhetoric. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-15 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-declares-free-safe-environment-for-journalists-under-bagong-pilipinas/ | 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Positive / mixed | The administration said DICT and the NSC were investigating a manipulated deepfake and considering legal action. That is a legal/institutional response, not an obvious politicized purge or loyalty test. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-26 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/ | 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2 |
| Positive | Marcos pushed procurement reform to shorten timelines, standardize forms, and institutionalize e-procurement. That is evidence against using public resources as a pure patronage machine. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/ | 4B.5, 4B.4, 4B.2 |
| Positive / mixed | Marcos reorganized the National Security Council into a more resilient institution with cabinet, legislative, military, intelligence, and legal members. That is institutional governance rather than a plainly loyalist personal circle, though it still centralizes discretion. | Lawphil / Office of the President | 2024-12-30 | https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_81_2024.html | 4B.5, 4B.4, 3B.9, 4B.2 |
| Positive / mixed | The administration expanded eFOI access and maintained media-literacy/disinformation efforts. That supports a limited transparency posture rather than closed, personality-centered rule. | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-18 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036 | 4B.5, 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2 |
| Negative | HRW said red-tagging under Marcos placed leftist activists and critics at serious risk, with officials and supporters accusing them of communist ties. That is inconsistent with a ruler who avoids politicizing neutral state power against critics. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Negative | HRW reported Marcos-era officials and police or military members repeatedly visited union leaders and threatened them by linking them to communism. This is direct intimidation of independent civil society, not neutral administration. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8 |
| Negative | The Reuters Institute says red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted under Marcos. That points to a coercive environment that can politicize supposedly neutral civic and media space. | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2 |
| Negative | Amnesty says Marcos-era actors weaponized digital tools, misinformation, and anti-terror framing to create fear, and that red-tagging vilified activists, journalists, teachers, and others. This is strong evidence against clean separation between state and partisan intimidation. | Amnesty International | 2024-10-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/ | 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Negative | Freedom House says elections are free from overt restrictions but not fully fair because disinformation and vote buying distort competition; it also says red-tagging persisted under Marcos. This is broad evidence that neutral institutions were not fully insulated from politicization. | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024 | 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Negative | The U.S. State Department report says credible killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, media restrictions, and threats to labor activists remained. That is not consistent with a cleanly depoliticized state apparatus. | U.S. State Department via ecoi.net | 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html | 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.1 |

**Bottom line:** there is some evidence of institutional respect and administrative modernization, but the stronger 2024 record still includes red-tagging and coercive pressure on critics, journalists, and labor organizers. That makes it hard to say Marcos clearly avoided politicizing neutral institutions.

**Search gap:** I did not find strong 2024 evidence of formal loyalty tests, compulsory personality-cult rituals, or systematic party capture in the narrow sense. The evidence is much stronger on intimidation/red-tagging and weaker on explicit cult-building.
